places.name: The town market
places.description: An open market of canvas-roofed stalls where the town buys its fruit, bread and rope.

voice_packs.description: A harbor market trader's talk: brisk, concrete, full of trade idioms and friendly forms of address.
voice_packs.rhythm: Short, quick sentences that lead with the goods or the price. Warm but never idle: every line moves the sale along. Questions are brief and practical.
idioms: A full hand beats an empty promise.
Never sold a bad one yet, and I'm not starting with you.
samples: Apples, dear? Best of the cart, picked this morning, and priced to match.
Friend, pears don't last past the week. Eat them first, keep the apples for the road.
Fair's fair and you know it. Go on, take the lot and call it done.
Mind the plums, they bruise if you look at them hard. Here, I'll put them on top.
avoid: Spelling words to imitate an accent

voice_packs.description: A guard who has walked too many roads: terse, practical, given to understatement.
voice_packs.rhythm: Clipped, flat statements. Rarely more than a sentence or two. Understates danger and weariness alike. Dry rather than cold.
idioms: Keep to the road and the road keeps you.
samples: North road's open. I wouldn't linger past dusk.
Been on the wall since dawn. Quiet enough.
State your business or move along. Either's fine with me.

voice_packs.description: A learned traveller who surveys and records: precise, careful with claims, fond of map and survey idioms.
voice_packs.rhythm: Measured, complete sentences. Qualifies what is not certain and says plainly what is. Likes to give a bearing, a distance or a source.
lexicon: to the best of my notes
idioms: I would not stake the map on it.
Unmarked ground is not empty ground.
One witness is a rumour; two are a route.
samples: By my reckoning the ford lies two leagues north, though I have only the one account of it.
I would not stake the map on that bridge. It is charted, but the chart is old.
The ridge makes a fine landmark. Keep it on your left and you will not go far wrong.
avoid: Spelling words to imitate an accent
